gaps.sentence: It was Marie Curie ___ discoveries changed modern medicine.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose discoveries' means 'Marie Curie's discoveries'; 'who's' would mean 'who is'.

gaps.sentence: 1998 was the year ___ the factory finally closed.
That's exactly ___ I needed — thank you!
gaps.explanation: 'What I needed' means 'the thing that I needed'; 'that' cannot be used in this free relative position.

gaps.sentence: There are times ___ I really miss my home town.
gaps.explanation: 'There are times when ...' is a standard pattern; 'when' stands for 'at which'.

gaps.sentence: This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which' and needs no preposition; 'the hotel which we stayed' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: There are cases ___ this rule simply does not apply.
gaps.explanation: 'Cases where ...' means 'cases in which ...'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause without a subject.

gaps.sentence: Nobody explained the reason ___ the flight was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Why' introduces the cause after 'the reason'; it means 'for which'.
